risk_of_bias.note: High is right and equals the worst domains. One point for the senior author: the instrument fit is weak. METHODS 5.3 reserves RoB 2 for randomized or counterbalanced designs, and this is a fixed-order, subject-blind administration study, so RoB 2's randomization domain is being used to record the absence of the very feature that makes the instrument apply. The card's own domain note says as much. The design enum and scripts/rob_vocab.py map human-laboratory to RoB 2, so the card is internally valid; the choice is between documenting the exception on the card and re-appraising with ROBINS-I (non-randomized study of an intervention).

risk_of_bias_domains.note: No randomization at all: 10 mg first for everyone, 20 mg three weeks later for the five who remained (p. 122).
Subject-blind with placebo capsules, dosing supervised on a closed ward; staff blinding not described.
Three of eight did not reach the second regimen, one had no plasma after the first dose, one no physiological data; high fits.

Validated assay with duplicate controls in each batch. The oral-fluid pH resolution of 0.4 units is coarse for a pH-dependent outcome, but pH is an explanatory variable, not the outcome, so low still fits.
No protocol; two of three collection methods only in an online supplement; the model parameters printed twice with different values.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor is right: the conclusions about oral fluid against urine follow from the data, and the card's two cautions (formulation-dependent time to peak, five participants behind the physiological findings) are the real limits.
